<reason>PRO's adjustable-logistics versus unadjustable-biology asymmetry survived the exchange. CON needed bedtimes to shift a full hour to erase the gain, while PRO persuasively argued even partial, better-timed sleep counts and answered the supervision concern with teenage self-care and early non-instructional drop-off. CON's economic harms were serious, but its claimed total bedtime cancellation and local alternatives never provided an enforceable protection against early starts.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: it directly answered both pressure questions, showed partial bedtime drift does not equal relocated deprivation, and distinguished an 8:30 instructional start from schools opening earlier for supervised drop-off.</best_rebuttal>
